reviews.text: Chaotic, decadent, and packed to the gills with movie-making madness, this is a love-or-hate viewing experience.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: Babylon is an adrenaline rush from start to finish, with said rush being raunchy, hilarious, powerful, confounding, just about anything you can imagine.
reviews.author: Branyan Towe

reviews.text: Babylon is a story about people who want to be stars, become stars, and are ultimately reduced to stardust.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: Ultimately a condemnation of the Hollywood machine that crushes everyone with equitable cruelty and an ode to the innovative artistry and ineffable magic of the movies, whose siren call continues to lure audiences & filmmakers alike towards its warm glow.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: Babylon isn't all bust, or even unwatchable, it is just overlong, overindulgent with nary a care...
reviews.author: Manik Sharma

reviews.text: Babylon is provocative, but, at the same time, it highlights what almost serves as a thematic watermark in Chazelle's filmography: choosing success often means choosing suffering or torture. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nicolás Medina

reviews.text: Unsure if my brain will ever fully heal from what Chazelle goes-for-broke with in the extended finale, but one thing is certain: audiences may very well never see anything like it ever again. Whether that’s for better or worse is up to the viewer...
reviews.author: Alex Papaioannou

reviews.text: Babylon is built on the idea that the primary goal of the film world is to make the viewer feel something even if it is disgust and pity.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: All-embracing, all-consuming, and yet wholly intimate, Chazelle’s masterful epic is not only an ode to where film came from but where it will further journey to continue capturing our hearts, minds, and souls.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: An eyeball-searing trip into a version of writer-director Chazelle’s Hollywood.
reviews.author: Mini Anthikad-Chhibber

reviews.text: Babylon’ goes big and refuses to be ignored, even if a much better, much shorter movie exists somewhere inside the messy sprawl.
reviews.author: Greg Carlson

reviews.text: Movie lovers will take to "Babylon" with a great deal of admiration, while others might struggle to notice how much it resonates within the film industry as part of historical importance.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle’s Love Letter to Hollywood, Movies, Filmmaking, & its stars. A beautiful, hilarious, insane, ride through the debauchery of Hollywood & the stunning aspects of making a film. Wolf of Wall Street meets Hollywood. I LOVED it.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Chazelle cracks the fantasy facade of the film by breaking down the moving images into a collection of frames and solid colors that make us question how we actually perceive the screen.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: Babylon is pure excess, to its own detriment. Chazelle became so lost in frolicking in the playground of the 1920s Hollywood he’s created that he forgot to tie it all together into something meaningful.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Babylon is a visual feast full of committed performances, charting years of the start of Hollywood’s Golden Age with all involved clearly having a riot.
reviews.author: Christopher Connor

reviews.text: Chazelle frames it as a tragicomic exercise that underscores power dynamics and the filmmaking process in a golden age of Hollywood cloaked in frenzy, elegance and fading stars on the brink of the abyss. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Repulsive, wretched excess...
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Chazelle seems to have abandoned the moving humanism that animated his early films, opting instead to wallow in grotesquerie, absurdity, and debauchery
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: A fascinating mess.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Babylon is ambitious, and costly—and almost a complete shambles. It is badly constructed and unconvincingly done, providing little or no insight into the film industry, culture in general or American society.
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: For all that is great and grand in its use of history, the film is long and you can feel it, a problem when making an epic.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: As it stands, after two movies that started the “White People Freaking Out About Jazz” genre, I don’t have a lot of faith in Chazelle telling these stories and Babylon has shown me that my fears were founded.
reviews.author: Stacey Yvonne

reviews.text: Babylon’s sound-recording scene replicates Singin’ in the Rain’s as something dire and unfunny and way too long.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: A filthy, funny, frenetic film that might be the weirdest holiday-season release in recent memory.
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: The writing utilises pitch black humour to lambast a terrible system while still sincerely acknowledging the beauty of the artform.
reviews.author: Gemma Creagh

reviews.text: Chazelle appears to have mistaken his own dexterity for directing.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Babylon is an easy film to hate. Chazelle’s work is sloppy, arrogant, and self-indulgent bordering on masturbatory, but also irritatingly beautiful and hard to get out of one’s head.
reviews.author: Ian Thomas Malone

reviews.text: Outside of these production moments, the film feels like it’s toiling away at revealing plot threads that aren’t nearly as engaging as they could be.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: Surely there came a point in this extravaganza when the director, the producers, the actors, and the people who did the catering, began to feel it had all gone wrong.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: Chazelle’s overstuffed homage to old Hollywood is often totally bonkers, but it’s also consistently mesmerizing. Running longer than 3 hours, it's an undeniably self-indulgent exercise, but one that showcases magnificent craftsmanship at every level.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: It may have been a box office failure, but all three hours are utilized perfectly and never goes flat.
reviews.author: Brian Susbielles

reviews.text: Babylon is as chaotic and messy as what it tries to describe, but it's wonderful, and manages to make us reflect on the implications of fame, with its moments of glory and decline. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: The back half of the film, while it does have its highlights, demonstrates an inability for the movie to fully carry its own weight, and the multi-faceted narrative descends into tropes and some groan-worthy material before the end credits start to roll.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: With Babylon, though, Chazelle gives us magic, but trumps it with sheer, unadulterated madness.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: There’s nothing personal or profound in this messy imagination of the early movies; it’s just a spectacle reduced to tics and gimmicks.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle’s bonkers biopic about the excess of Old Hollywood will bowl you over in the best way, but it might leave you scratching your head in confusion too
reviews.author: Alex Flood

reviews.text: [Babylon] is a bumpy ride but rarely feels tedious.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: So bad it's shocking.  Such of waste of acting talent.  This is what happens when Hollywood calls someone a genuis and lets them create without ever having to think twice about any of their decisions.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: This is an absolutely repugnant masterpiece. It is a romantic nightmare. It is bat-shit crazy. And I loved every last second of it.
reviews.author: Dave Lee

reviews.text: Babylon lurches from moment to moment. It is full of half-ideas but lacking in the imagination to do much with it. Instead, it feigns jocularity while feeling unspontaneous and unnatural in its convulsions, too studied and tedious to excite.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: Attempts to out-Fellini Fellini are regrettable and for much of its length Babylon is an unsubtle and indigestible mess so that despite all the talent involved and the fascinating subject matter, it must be seen as something of a disaster.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: A more ruthless editor could easily have stream-lined a stronger piece, but as it stands it’s a bedazzling screech of a film that threw restraint out the window, where it landed in a pile of Robbie’s vomit on a designer rug. It’s bonkers.
reviews.author: Ben Turner

reviews.text: A relentless and ravenous movie that's always a lot, not just in length, but is dazzling (and also very funny) when it clicks.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Judged against Chazelle’s previous work, Babylon lacks the edge of Whiplash, the heart of La La Land, and the focus of First Man. Such a well-versed student of cinema should know better than to fall into self-indulgence.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: A prurient, celebratory, confused, scandalized, and sad celebration of the notion of Old Hollywood as a place of incomparable possibility and freedom.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: At its best, Babylon is indecently good fun.
reviews.author: Nick Hasted

reviews.text: ... An intense tribute to cinema that delights hard-core cinephiles. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Lara

reviews.text: It's a different kind of Damien Chazelle film. It's more cynical, it's more mean-spirited, in fact it almost feels like a response to LA LA LAND and what happened after that film's notorious "win" at the Oscars.
reviews.author: Brendan Cassidy

reviews.text: An artistic melting pot. Babylon is an uneven and disorganized film in line with the Hollywood carousel of cheap impressions that spins in all directions yet never bets on any. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: Subtle it is not. Nor is it good.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Blah-blah land.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Watching the film is like riding a rollercoaster in a storm of images, lifted on the rhythms of Justin Hurwitz’s compelling score.
reviews.author: Ayelet Dekel

reviews.text: If anything, Babylon is too good a recreation of late-silent era Hollywood – it’s self-indulgent, overwrought, underwritten, and following a full-frontal assault on the senses, peters out into irrelevance.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: Chazelle’s film commemorates the era’s hubris as it indulges in a bit of its own.  This is how a world ends. Not with a whimper but a great deal of banging, baby. And vomiting. And snorting.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: I staggered out trying to shake off not just the onset of cramp, but also the vague, dispiriting sense that I'd just been hoodwinked by the ending into thinking that Babylon is a better film than it is.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: An exercise of superlative narcissism that's as hollow as it's irritating and amorphous. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Beatriz Martínez

reviews.text: As uneven as it is magnetic, Babylon is an essential chute in which Margot Robbie and Brad Pitt not only know they are the brightest stars in the sky but they make it clear that they have enjoyed it... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Rosado

reviews.text: Much ado about nothing. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: Those willing to put up with various scenes of decadence, asking us to step into an unpleasant world, will find a film that says a lot about the way fame affects people, and how they try to find something that feels fulfilling. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: It's fascinating, exciting, and wild, though it isn't hard to understand why it failed theatrically in the United States. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Chazelle struggles to make a coherent point about the morality of show business.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: Babylon is a disaster of biblical proportions, precisely because it had so much potential.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Babylon approaches the creation of set-piece moments and vast, crowded scenes with commendable gusto, but lacks subtlety and rarely dips below its own glittering surface.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Despite trying to recapture an important moment in Hollywood history, Babylon gets stuck with a sense of humor without depth. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Susana Guzman De la O

reviews.text: Babylon is an excessive, impudent, visceral film; it is an extraordinary movie. Like any good declaration of love. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: ... A film that has as many pretenses as resources, but ultimately fails because every time it reaches a peak, it tends to deflate and drift. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Babylon is not so much a film of two halves, but a third of a brilliant movie and two hours of unmitigated mess and chaos.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: …Babylon is a big, chunky, entertainingly lavish and deliberately obsessive train-set, but despite considerable effort, it remains an indulgent plaything…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: The film feels like a terrific two-hour film crammed into three hours, the first of which is full of fits and starts. The direction is haphazard, toggling between wildness and tedium, resulting in characterizations that are thin and hard to care about.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: 'Babylon' is somehow both many things. It's grotesque yet gorgeous. It's obscene yet opulent. It's baffling yet bold. It's repugnant yet resplendent. It's hollow yet heartfelt. Fortune favours the brave and Chazelle isn't playing it safe here.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: In the end, Chazelle does evoke the elegiac mood he’s after, finishing with a wistful meditation on the evanescence of fame and the fragility of those who fail to survive its demands.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: While Babylon starts as a big, sloppy visual treat, it finishes as the cinematic equivalent of a pile of dung.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: The cast's commitment is extraordinary, especially Robbie's, a true force of nature, and Pitt's, to whom Chazelle devotes his most indulgent gaze. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: If this is what failure looks like, then let's have more of it. I'd rather see a film that fails this boldly, than one that succeeds meekly, any day at all.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: The three protagonists carry the weight of the story, which comes with a few surprises. Each of them has a scene to shine. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: The tragi-comedy is an epic of decadence and depravity. It is crude, profligate and staggeringly audacious, but there is never any doubting Chazelle’s heady passion for the movies however ugly the business.
reviews.author: Whang Yee Ling

reviews.text: The film ultimately offers something like a square's take on Hollywood as seen through the eyes of Kenneth Anger.
reviews.author: Keva York

reviews.text: The composition of Babylon is a masterpiece in production, including costume, music, cinematography -- and yet, there is something missing in the mélange.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: Fascinating, heart-breaking, laugh out loud and consistently entertaining. Babylon is evidently not for everyone... but those who'll love it, will truly love, warts and all.
reviews.author: Bren Murphy

reviews.text: As a movie monument to movie-making itself, Babylon served me up some unforgettable moments and his grand finale catapulted me out of the cinema.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: Is it entertaining though? Yes, yes, absolutely yes. Despite content and quality and length and being kinda bad and dumb. Despite everything, Babylon is undeniably captivating.
reviews.author: Amelia Berry

reviews.text: Each image is there to offend, to attract attention, and perhaps to irritate. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: If the running time is a tribute to 1920s excess, Chazelle should have listened harder to his old ghosts. Kid, you’re meant to leave ’em wanting more.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Chazelle has come up with a handful of striking sequences, padded out with a whole lot of artfully directed filler making the case that - aside from a few memorable moments - the history of cinema is just a bunch of sound and fury signifying nothing.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: A scabrous takedown of Tinsel Town's worst excesses in the 1920s... the run time does fizzle out and it gets a bit cheesy
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: I didn't buy one second of it, for one moment.
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: I absolutely loved it... What [Damien Chazelle] does that I love is tell the story in such an exaggerated, maniacal fashion that it feels truer than it's ever felt before.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Babylon is an epic, exceptional, dynamic, in your face, chaotically wild and ultimately tragic journey through decades of filmmaking from 1920s Hollywood ... a cinematic work of art ... Babylon is that brash, bolder, bigger story compared to La La Land
reviews.author: Latoya Austin

reviews.text: A spectacularly long, grossly indulgent, hilariously vile ode to cinema that stands as the filmmaker’s most ambitious and divisive project to date.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Though it’s supposed to inspire awe at how far movies have come, all it really does is showcase the extent to which Chazelle relies on other movies to compensate for this film’s deficiencies, which are evident from the off.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: A triumphant, bold, and hypervitalized celebration of the big screen. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Philipp Engel

reviews.text: For a director skilled at mounting set-pieces, Chazelle is extraordinarily duff at managing structure on a larger scale: perhaps those talents don’t sit well together. Babylon has spectacular scenes yet is hopelessly unwieldy as a whole.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: Audacious, sensational and uncompromising, Babylon might be Chazelle’s best and worst film. We should be grateful such ballsy filmmakers still work within the confines of Hollywood.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: Sleazy yet high-brow, the film is going to struggle to find an audience, but one suspects that it will be endlessly critically re-evaluated.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: Babylon is a synapse-frazzling extravaganza, a libidinous bacchanal of writhing bodies, coke-dusted noses and lurid sex acts.
reviews.author: Yasmin Omar

reviews.text: While there are some notable shortcomings which holds it back from being Chazelle’s best, Babylon is a wild, manic ride in its tribute to cinema. It won’t be for everyone, but you applaud its ambition.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: Babylon itself is pure cinema, it’s an explosion of filmmaking by a director cutting loose and going hell for leather but it is also disjointed, uncurbed and not always enjoyable - the excess BECAME excessive and the delirium made ME delirious.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: Whatever amazements the movie offers initially are ground down into weariness. It's a chore.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Wunderkind Chazelle seriously needs artistic supervision. Babylon is the first Millennial film so misguided that it seems hell-bent on destroying itself.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: For all Babylon’s excess, Chazelle’s self-consciously virtuosic style saps the life from even its most overcrowded tableaux.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: Babylon was ambitious, but unfortunately it was too much noise and just didn't work.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: An overwhelming yet dazzling rollercoaster through its grandiose production, bold direction and endearing characters.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle deftly captures the frenetic atmosphere of early Hollywood, the fatal fumbles of new technology, and the tragic decline of studios, actors, and careers without losing himself or the picture in the details
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: Among all its brilliance, the best quality of “Babylon” is its spot-on exploration of cultural assimilation in Hollywood. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: ... Rarely do projects as ambitious as 'Babylon' manage to be so much fun. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: I'm willing to overlook Babylon's messy self-indulgence in favour of the maudlin romp it's meant to be.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: Babylon plays out like Damien Chazelle spent his lockdown listening to Karina Longworth’s “You Must Remember This” podcast, only to realize he could make his version of Boogie Nights from that material.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: It’s unquestionably Chazelle’s biggest movie, and while it might not have the same crowd-pleasing impact of “Whiplash” or “La La Land,” it also might be the best distillation yet of how and why this particular director makes movies.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: While the performances are outstanding and the movie-making scenes are often exquisite, the hedonism and debauchery of Babylon feels like a completely different movie that serves, essentially, as a MacGuffin to connect the characters.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: Babylon tries, and manages, to paint both the heaven and the hell of cinema, of creators, and of fame and fortune. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Powerful, hilarious and bleak as hell.
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: It’s not really clear what Damien Chazelle is trying to accomplish in his latest, Babylon. The movie is so awful that he should probably be banished from Hollywood.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: It's foul (in language and actions), it's excessive and it's fantastic.
reviews.author: Michael Balderston

reviews.text: Chazelle is so flagrantly trying to have his cake and eat it too that it’s almost hard to get upset or annoyed at him or his film; I feel the need to grant him points for pure audacity.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: If LA LA LAND was a love letter to the magic of making movies, this is like hate mail.. with Chazelle showing how the industry treats people as disposable and ruins lives.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: He rattled off three masterpieces with the gritty drumming drama “Whiplash” (2014), the nostalgic musical romance “La La Land” (2016) and the underrated space biopic “First Man” (2018), but there must come a time that even Damien Chazelle soils the bed.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: This outrageous, obnoxious, overstuffed epic about early Hollywood’s debauchery is nothing short of a disastrous masterpiece. Sort of.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: The rare three-hour movie you could watch twice in a row.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: As breathtakingly beautiful as this film is to watch, if falls a bit flat on character development except for Manny Torres, gorgeously portrayed by Diego Calva.  Three hours didn't bother me but not exploring racism with actors and directing sexism did.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: It’s the most glamorous film about how unglamorous filmmaking is ever made.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Flashy & fatiguing, it's grotesquely graphic - a three-hour mess of a movie. Too bad the over-the-top craftsmanship of cinematographer Linus Sandgren, production designer Florencia Martin, costumer Mary ZXophres, and editor Tom Cross is simply squandered.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Babylon deserves so much better. Hope you all enjoyed Avatar 2 while this absolutely brilliant film dies at the box office.
reviews.author: Adam Olinger

reviews.text:
Pitt and Robbie are good actors. They’re not miracle workers. Calva tries, but when you’re stuck behind an elephant, the results aren’t always good.

That’s “Babylon,” a big-budget free-for-all that should have tamed the beast, not upset it.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: If La La Land represented Chazelle in his high school freshman era, then Babylon is him as a college senior desperate to graduate.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: It is quite ironic that the same excessive, overwrought scenario that Chazelle is painting a visually stunning picture of here, is also the same overindulgence that dooms Babylon from becoming the masterpiece it deserved to be.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: The three-hour runtime is the least of this frantic, loud film’s egregious excesses...
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: It's long, all over the place, unsure of its message & is over exaggerated. BUT I really enjoyed it a lot more than I thought I would! It has some very strong moments, well acted scenes & dissects levels of negatives/positives of created cinema
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: Under Chazelle’s bruised showman sensibility, to love something means honestly seeing all the ways in which it is broken and still hearing violins when you look at it anyway.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: Despite some really fine performances the film remains emotionally neutral. We may be diverted by these characters, but we’re not moved by them; their downfalls seem less tragic than a case of just desserts.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: It is an epic of decadence devolving into degradation, if a flawed one, bursting with the affection Chazelle so obviously has for the process of filmmaking that can sometimes be fatal.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Out of the collision of love and hate stems a volatile and audacious film where subtlety is extinct and the excesses multiply with every scene. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: Chazelle takes three hours and nine minutes to bring Babylon to its predictably ironic conclusion. As I watched the film, I wondered exactly what Chazelle had in mind...
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: In Babylon, film is a medium born of light and shadow built on ashes and ruined dreams that become something beautiful and immortal. That tension makes up the film's central conflict, daring to ask - is it all worth it?
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: It’s a big, boisterous, brash mess. But the stars shine so bright, the music pumps so loud and the crash hits so hard that the film emerges a somewhat battered winner.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: At times, you wonder if it should have been called “Babble On.” It certainly does that. And although not a deadly sin, beware the urge to repent.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: “Babylon” is a cumbersome mess from writer-director Damien Chazelle, who has crafted pretty images – and some disgusting things that you can’t unsee — in a story without heart or soul.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: An overstuffed, overindulgent ode to cinema that throws a lot at the audience, but when it hits (and it does it a lot in the 189 minute run time), it really flies.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Unfortunately for audiences, there’s only so much fine fabrics and gilded chandeliers can do. The film struggles to maintain any semblance of pace and there is distinct impression that the movie did not know how to end.
reviews.author: Terence Johnson

reviews.text: One of the year’s richest and most ambitious films.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Chazelle is trying to make a point with all the excess... I’m not sure if I agree or if I was simply beaten into submission after more than three hours, but Babylon is the kind of grandiose folly that at least gives the viewer a big old mess to chew on.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Its panache begins to feel more like the idea of panache -- like a bodysnatcher lurking under a skin of actual cinematic style, all empty gestures and wiry nothingness. The disappointment is that the movie wields so much and achieves so relatively little.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Despite a stellar cast and showy moments (given who’s involved how could there not be?), the writer-director’s sprawling, messy, three-hour-plus endurance test isn’t ready for its closeup.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle tries to cover too much and winds up stretching a lot of his ideas too thin.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: This film throws an enticing party, but offers nothing for the morning after except the hangover of its length.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: It's all too much, and too predictable to rise up as transcendentally as Chazelle clearly hopes it will. It's a lot of time, effort, and money to bring us a story that has already happened countless times before.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: Babylon is a profoundly humanist film, mourning the tragedies that litter Hollywood histories. But it’s also a worshipful film, one that gladly buys into the dream, the spell, the mystery of it all.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Bloated with extraneous scenes that double down on the debauchery shock and awe instead of giving the characters more depth. It's too bad as the talented cast is committed and did their best to keep it engaging.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: The performances are fun, the music raucous, the costumes glorious. And yet, the entire visual feast of a movie recalls the excessive party scene in Baz Luhrmann's overstuffed The Great Gatsby, beautiful and damned.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: Without any subtlety or ambiguity, Babylon feels like a movie that wants to be the “most” movie of 2022. It’s hard to argue against the exciting highs of this film. However, the lows will make you wish you were watching anything else.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Writer-director Damien Chazelle creates enough visual panache to hold the attention for three hours, even if some plot strands feel like overwrought sideroads. But it's also a dazzling take on the true cost of moviemaking.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: A glorious mess. This may be just for film historians, arguably a limited audience, as this R-rated SINGING THE RAIN has Brad representing John Gilbert and Margot as Clara Bow. Worth seeing for a look at a film biz that will never exist that way again.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle's new Hollywood epic is full of excess. Sometimes, to a fault.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: What’s really, truly embarrassing is how completely sure Damien Chazelle is that he’s absolutely nailing every scene in this movie.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: Revels in its deafeningly loud, obnoxious, unrelenting pace and fetish for excess.
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: The first 90 minutes are an instant classic in the making; unfortunately, it continues for another 90 minutes
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: An angry and hostile film.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Chazelle’s showoff moves are all clumsy imitation and pastiche.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: It is too much and often, especially in call-outs to "Singin' In The Rain," a little on the nose. It is also clearly heartfelt and that counts.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: If many of its players aren’t done justice, the love of the medium itself is undeniable.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: It’s an attentive interpretation of the history of the period, refined and emboldened by the deeply personal human reasons that people are drawn both to the cinema and to the environs of cinema-making.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: Without question, “Babylon” is a flawed film, a bloated piece of work that doesn’t completely succeed. Yet, it’s a grand swing for the fences and while the filmmaker doesn’t hit it out of the park, the result is worthwhile, nonetheless.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The film’s final moments, set in a 1930s movie palace, is a daring artistic leap but is wholly dependent on a sweep of feeling that the filmmaker, despite his many gifts, and three hours of razzle dazzle, hasn’t managed to conjure.
reviews.author: Chuck Wilson

reviews.text: Through all its filth, cynicism and poison-inked vengeance, Babylon cannot help but to be a devoted worshiper at the altar of cinema—and its admiration proves infectious.
reviews.author: Kathy Michelle Chacón

reviews.text: The first 60 minutes of wunderkind director Damien Chazelle's latest three-hour razzle-dazzle is a frenetic masterpiece of lust and probably everything anyone thinks they know about what goes on in Hollywood, even now.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: ...hit-and-miss yet mostly engaging...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: After a really strong first half, Damien Chazelle’s film reveals its hand as less a serious indictment of the Hollywood dream factory and more of a shallow spin on ‘technology kills actors’ that owes more to the structure of Boogie Nights than its content
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: An exhausting, nihilistic, shallow, overlong and conflicting non-story, but hey the costumes are great.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: It certainly makes a statement and will be talked about, especially over awards season. Go in with an open mind and extra time on your hands and be prepared for the wildest movie of the season.
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: Loaded with vulgarity, passion, and energy, Babylon is one big party of an intoxicating cinema explosion.
reviews.author: Mark McPherson

reviews.text: I didn’t love Babylon but I can’t condemn it either. How could I when its finale is a love letter to movies and the way they can lift our spirits? Any filmmaker who strives for that shouldn’t be dismissed, even if he made us sit still for over three hours
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: Babylon is essentially Singin’ in the Rain remade as The Wolf of Wall Street, and it is every bit as exhilarating and exhausting as that sounds.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: The performances are good, as is much of the dialogue, and I imagine this will be a contender in multiple categories for the various 2022 movie awards.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: This epic spectacle embraces the over-the-top opulence of a burgeoning 1920s movie industry awash in depravity and scandal, while also skillfully weaving in a more grounded character-driven tale of transition and personal struggle.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: One way to describe the film would be a visual feast, yes, but another way to describe it would be a hearty mess.
reviews.author: Lex Briscuso

reviews.text: You can enjoy its garish pageant of sex, drugs, death, and screaming matches while still wondering if Chazelle is cosplaying transgression, trying to will himself into a rock star of American coke-binge cinema.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle’s Babylon is a classic Hollywood reflection on itself at a pivotal point in its history, chronicling the rise and subsequent fall of a series of characters at different points in the journeys to stardom.
reviews.author: Adam Mullins-Khatib

reviews.text: A frustrating, glorious, messy epic.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: "Babylon" is exasperating. It tries to do too much but ends up doing not saying very little. Less would have been more.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: Self-indulgent, stomach-churning...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: The prevailing attitude of Babylon is baseless, adolescent snark and misplaced superiority masquerading as humility. It's Bardo again, but less well-read.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: If you’re brave enough to commit to that monstrous runtime, Chazelle does little to make it worth your investment.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: ...it's hard not to compare Margot Robbie and Brad Pitt in Babylon with the more three-dimensional characters they played in Quentin Tarantino's superior 2019 Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood.
reviews.author: Kathy Fennessy

reviews.text: There’s been a lot of talk about the death of the movies lately, but Babylon’s two paddles to its heart. Muy awooga. For awhile, at least.
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: Get by the lurid first act then you'll find Babylon's value. So an hour of scatological/genital dreck and two hours of darkness .. replacing jolts per second. Chazelle's runaway style and scattershot focus are deeply distracting.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Brad Pitt and Margo Robbie headline Damien Chazelle’s colorful, frenetic and emotionally empty look at the excesses of silent-era Hollywood.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: The story that wraps around Jack, Manny, Nellie, and Elinor runs 188-minutes and I never felt its length. The movie breathes. It’s bravura filmmaking with imagination, depth, and spectacular production values.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle's Babylon is a train wreck, an ambitious and self-indulgent spectacular, that doesn't even try to corral all its disparate elements together into anything coherent.
reviews.author: Michelle Kisner

reviews.text: Its go-for-broke 40-minute pre-credit 1926 bacchanal must set some sort of record for most baroque lunacy in a studio film.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: Long and frequently unpleasant, but at least there’s a point to all that decadence and despair: first time as tragedy, second time as hit musical.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: An excessive, depraved and hysterical frenzy about the ephemeral nature of fame and the everlasting legacy of film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Chazelle can’t seem to land on whether or not he wants to reject nostalgia or eulogize cinema, and ultimately, it’s all incredibly smug for a message, and a movie, so muddled.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: The problem is that instead of giving us sincere pathos to accompany the illusionary imagery, Chazelle’s exaggerated and anarchic impulses overwhelm us.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: With all the intimate and poignant films this year about filmmaking and the industry itself, Chazelle’s is undoubtedly the loudest but also the most unaffecting.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: Decadence shouldn't be such a chore to sit through.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: Babylon will divide audiences, but Chazelle continues to show his worth in the industry with his strong eye and control.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: There's about an hour of terrific movie in this love-hate look at lurid Old Hollywood. Too bad it’s trapped in three hours of self-indulgent bloat. Even the starshine of Robbie and Pitt dissipates as Damien Chazelle rabidly bites the hand that feeds him.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Will this come to be known as Damien Chazelle’s folly? I hope so.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: It goes nowhere, in a mad rush.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: "Babylon" deserves credit for taking big swings, but it's usually unclear what it's swinging at.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: “Babylon” is a labor of love that never feels laborious. But as the allusions and inside jokes pile up, they become distracting.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Chazelle whips the story into cream-puff whorls of myths upon myths. He delivers a movie that's neither unified nor disparate but homogenized, its elements of reality and hyperbole alike assimilated to the same creamy glow of rueful wonder.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: The boisterous, brawling yet melancholy Babylon is a variation on film history, but more drawing for drama on its whispers, its rumors, as in suspect and spoiled texts.. gaudy and mean... It soars and splats, sings and moans...
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: While the director is a consummate craftsman who stages several staggering scenes of razzle-dazzle, it’s all pugnaciously heartless. To put it even more bluntly: I couldn’t have cared less.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Babylon exhibits some amusement with its unflinching depiction of unhinged Hollywood mayhem, but even that gets tiresome after a while. Babylon quickly becomes a bloated slog that loses sight of its core.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: It’s as if this re-creation of 1920s Hollywood has been feverishly whipped up by a precocious 13-year-old boy with a dirty mind and a generous allowance.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: Babylon is a sensory overload of boisterous energy and one of the most epic movie events of the year. Chazelle successfully captures both a changing industry and city in his own raw, dirty and destructive Singin’ in the Rain.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: “Babylon” is way too much and not enough at the same time.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Chazelle seems less interested in the artistic and commercial upheaval that accompanied the decline of silent films than he is in the debauched behavior of his characters.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: This ambivalence is, in and of itself, a point of interest, since most movies made at Babylon’s budget level are afraid to put any onus of interpretation on the audience. But it’s also risky.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Watching Damien Chazelle’s 'Babylon' may be as close as we’ll get to seeing a blown-out version of the “tunnel of terror” sequence in 1971’s 'Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory.' It's spectacularly wild and hilarious!
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Vivid, colorful, striking, and fascinating with massive sets, ear grabbing music, and front-line stars like Brad Pitt and Margot Robbie, Babylon goes all out with top quality production,
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: Chazelle has hinted at some of the bravura filmmaking seen in Babylon in his prior films ... but those moments were simply appetizers compared to the main course here.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: Chazelle can be weirdly inattentive to the overall structure of a movie’s narrative, so that, while never boring, Babylon winds up being exhausting.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: An overstuffed and -- especially by the increasingly wayward third act -- meandering film. But it’s also an insistently alive one that’s hard to look away from, with flashes of brilliance.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: (Another) film about movies in a year full of films about movies...  a few memorable moments are all viewers receive from a plot championing chewing up people’s lives for the sake of entertainment — because hey, they wanted it, right?
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: This barnstorming entry into the excesses of early Hollywood is landmark cinema. Featuring some inspired performances from Margot Robbie, Brad Pitt, and Diego Luna, Babylon is worth every column inch of praise for Damien Chazelle.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: Throughout this disappointing movie, what’s missing is the one thing that defined the silent era at its greatest and to which Chazelle remains bafflingly oblivious: its art.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: It's a masterpiece...a messy, eye-opening, gross, massive masterpiece.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Frenetic as Babylon is, Chazelle himself remains clear-eyed.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: Babylon loses itself in the excessiveness and never has a defining message that it wants the audience to walk away with.
reviews.author: Rosalie Kicks

reviews.text: Where the movie feels most alive is on the panicked film sets. One sequence even echoes the gags of Singin' in the Rain... but suddenly the idea of actors struggling with talking on camera is as brutal as the jazz-scored traumas in Chazelle's Whiplash.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: Though its style is positively hysterical, “Babylon” is elephantine in its effect—frantic but turgid, wildly over-the-top but drab and dull.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Overblown, risky, and compulsively watchable.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: As a whole ... Chazelle's movie lacks focus or any insight about the power of the movies and the perils of Hollywood that hasn't already been explored countless times.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Babylon isn't just a love letter to Classic Hollywood but one of the best movies of the year. It's a glorious Damien Chazelle masterpiece.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Babylon doesn’t feel “coked-out” so much as jittery and over-caffeinated. Given how thoughtlessly Chazelle wields images, and how carelessly he crafts their meaning, it’s hard to read his climactic ode as anything but a reminder that better movies exist.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Babylon is the kind of movie that reminds you why we love them in the first place.
reviews.author: Josie Meléndez

reviews.text: Love it or hate it, and there are valid reasons for either response, it is audacious, chaotic, vulgar, and, like its leading lady, it always makes a scene.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: There is a whole lot of enthusiasm both in front and behind the camera and that is a good thing, if somewhat tiring in the long (and I mean long) run.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: The title may explicitly refer to the licentiousness of 1920s Hollywood, but you could also apply it to the artistic degeneration of this misbegotten mess, made worse by the smug self-assurance of the mise-en-scène.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: I admire Chazelle’s ambition. He swings for the fences here -- and he’s obviously an enormously gifted director. But to me, this is a swing and a miss.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Don’t get me wrong, Chazelle creates some great things amid the welter, and he’s never boring, which is an achievement in such a long epic. Even so, this overstuffed exercise bites off more than it can chew.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Chazelle's reach exceeds his grasp. Scene after scene spins away, out of control, pumped full of eye-popping, blaring, empty hyperactivity.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: "Babylon" is a big movie. The stars are big, the sets are big, and the story is the story of cinema itself, culminating in one pornographic orgasm of image and sound so deafening the movie practically beats you into submission.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: One helluva cinema high! Costumes, characters, music, movie-making - all in excess & pleasure. Entertainingly messy, about the wonder & ugly of Hollywood. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Babylon is a movie about movies that’s made almost exclusively for movie lovers. It’s quite the ride with a lot of big ideas, some of them more fully formed than others.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: To drink in Chazelle’s mad brew of screwball vignettes and nostalgic yearning is to experience a transcendent high.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: This may be Chazelle’s love letter to Hollywood, but the envelope should be stamped return to sender.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: You're in for one of the most outlandishly energetic, sinful and ambitious cinematic experiences of this year.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: At the corner of 42nd Street and The Wolf of Wall Street, you’ll find Babylon. Oscar winner Damien Chazelle’s latest film takes aim at the industry itself, and is a spectacular bacchanal that will leave you disoriented and amazed.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Chazelle does a dazzling job of telling his story, even if for large swaths it's unclear if he's celebrating movie magic or driving a stake through Hollywood's heart. By the end it's clear... he's also a fanboy at heart.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Nearly all the main characters get a why-movies-matter monologue. Nearly all are shabbily written.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: It’s the only party in Hollywood that’s boozier, glitzier, and trashier than the Golden Globes. In this case, that’s high praise.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: Babylon does not love movies so much as it loves The Movies, an institution made up of... sultry signs that are meant to evoke that true but trite refrain, “they don’t make ‘em like they used to.”
reviews.author: Zach Lewis

reviews.text: It has a feverish energy that gets lost amid the reverie, and though it has a great cast, it takes too long to make a point as it meanders to its end.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: Babylon is a film too busy writing an elegy for the still-breathing body of film as a medium to capture the true beauty and complications of being alive.
reviews.author: Angelica Jade Bastién

reviews.text: A wild ride for a while, a star-studded, sprawling extravaganza, about Hollywood at the end of the silent era. But at a running length of just over three hours, it both makes its point, and overstays its welcome.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: “Babylon” may not be Chazelle’s “Heaven’s Gate,” exactly. But it’s definitely the most maddening movie experience you’ll have this year.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: A story about ego, chaos and excess that is pretentious, excessive and chaotic. More like “Once Upon a Time in a Malignant La La LAmsterdam.” {Full Review in Spanish)
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Chazelle’s three-plus-hour opus plays like a mocking homage to “Singin’ in the Rain” that, instead of highlighting song and dance, concentrates on tits, ass and drugs.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Traffics in riotous, bawdy, revolting excess. Prepare for orgies, drugs, alcohol, projectile vomiting, explosive defecating near and on individuals, plus gratuitous, pervasive cursing. And that’s just the first half of this three-hour plus extravaganza.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: A grueling filmgoing experience. It really does babble on and on and on and on. This is not a love letter to cinema, more like hate mail, odd coming from a director who has been treated well and lauded by his industry.
reviews.author: Pam Grady

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle stuffs a limited series worth of material into a wildly uneven yet undeniably entertaining 188 minutes detailing the depravity, ingenuity, talent and sheer luck that defined the early days of a surprisingly diverse Hollywood.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: After enduring — and I must say, enjoying much of — this wild and pungent cinematic bacchanal, I’m of the mind that they actually form a logical progression.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: There are so many adjectives one could use to describe Damien Chazelle’s Babylon; some good, some maybe not so good.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Babylon thins out all too quickly, settling for a strenuous ode to the dream factory and its victims and exploiters, who occasionally make wondrous things for the screen.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Despite its long run-time, and corny finish, Babylon is a complicated musical and visual spectacle with great performances by Robbie, Pitt, Smart and Clava in a frenetic film that left us more exhausted than exhilarated.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: “Babylon” is a fever dream of ecstasy that’s like if “The Great Gatsby” and “The Wolf of Wall Street” had a baby who loved doing cocaine.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Can’t bring the hazy stuff-for-stuff’s-sake into focus.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Brilliant at times, frustrating at others. A technically triumphant, but thinly plotted debauched journey into old Hollywood.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: There's much to enjoy about the unexpectedly freewheeling approach, but you sense the “party’s over” portion will similarly overcorrect into turgidity; call it "Singin’ in the Pain." That's exactly what "Babylon" does, spinning out into bumptious boredom.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle’s new Oscar-bait period-piece epic spins a sprawling, gloriously seedy tale about the deep-dish decadence of a bygone era.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Babylon is uneven, to be sure, but any missteps are more than compensated for by the exultation derived from the moments of frenetic exuberance that have become Chazelle’s bread-and-butter...
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: I both loved and hated it.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Babylon is not inherently “bad,” but for better or worse, it is a gaudy, brash display of the self-masturbatory nature of the film industry.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: Babylon is an overly long film that feels more strongly about capturing the vibes of 1920s Hollywood than actually telling a substantial story with a point and theme.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: But why opt for subtlety and insight when you can have upchuck and defecation?
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: Mostly exhausting, with Chazelle caught up in his ability to summon chaos, leaving little room for compelling drama to take shape.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: A lot of bells and whistles -- an admittedly superb acting -- amount to very little, in a movie whose plot about the downfall of great actors is mostly a rethread.
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: Owing much of its internal navigations to Stanley Donen, it’s a film which simultaneously feels like too much and yet not enough, but is, at times, so frenzied, it reaches a sense of zealous cinematic perfection.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: The first hour is atrocious...convoluted, meaningless, ridiculous. Worse, the sound is horrendous, deafening...a bloated orgiastic phantasmagoria, despite fine performances by Margot Robbie and Jean Smart
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: Babylon pours gasoline on a lewd fire of cinematic excess like a gleeful arsonist. Damien Chazelle throws restraint off a cliff to illustrate an era of unfettered debauchery. Not all of it works, but you're certainly not bored with the dazzling decadence.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Babylon is too stylish and packed with too many other strong aspects, yet it’s not quite the excellent take on 1920s La La Land that one would hope.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: A great score, a talented ensemble, and expert cinematography—all undeniable here. And yet there are narrative elements of “Babylon” that feel hollow from the very beginning and only get more so.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Yes, Babylon is, as its title more than hints at, A LOT. And I loved nearly every one of its unbelievable 188 minutes.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Despite running a whopping 186 minutes, the film whizzes by, thanks to its dazzling style, continually deepening story, and stellar performances.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: A messy, bloated epic about Hollywood’s early years, Babylon is more interested in shattering movie magic mythos than indulging in any. It spends the bulk of its time on behind-the-scenes grime—and rubbing our noses in it.
reviews.author: Valerie Kalfrin

reviews.text: A well-acted, but bloated, shallow, anarchic and consistently unpleasant mess that will make you want to take a long, cold shower afterwards.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: It’s not just a story about Hollywood — although yes, it is mostly that — but a story about how the things we build that are bigger than ourselves often don’t need us in the end.
reviews.author: Sarah Gorr

reviews.text: Three hours of pure cinematic kitchen sink energy, made with loving care.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: It’s supposed to be a frothy valentine to the industry but Chazelle’s comic sensibilities here are so heavy-handed and belligerent, it feels more like a Bronx cheer. Plus, he plays sloppily with period facts, and it makes this venture feel lazy.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Fueled by a frenetic --- and absolutely FABULOUS --- soundtrack, Damien Chazelle’s latest homage to Los Angeles, BABYLON, is about as bizarre and unexpected as one can imagine.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Margot Robbie renders a compelling performance of reckless abandon. She truly dances like no one is watching.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: So, I guess you CAN have too much of a good thing.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Babylon is as chaotic as one could imagine. Calva and Robbie are spectacular in this ambitious explosion of fast-paced madness. Chazelle’s darker take on Hollywood is fascinating, but he isn’t always able to balance so many storylines happening at once.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Recreating the unbridled hedonism of early Hollywood in a heady cocktail of sex, drugs, and iconic roles, Damien Chazelle’s indulgent three-hour epic Babylon is both a love letter to and cautionary tale of the excesses of cinema’s golden age.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: Much like the debauched parties in the film, [Damien] Chazelle's script is utterly chaotic and comes across like a tired imitation of Paul Thomas Anderson's 1997 masterpiece Boogie Nights.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: A fecal, anal honking, and vomit-infused tale revolving around orgy-driven slaphappiness and punchdrunk intoxication as the silent movie era disjointedly stumbled into sound and talkies. Babylon is an aggressive assault of the senses.
reviews.author: Chris Sawin

reviews.text: While the cast gives their all, Babylon's over-indulgence overstays its welcome and squanders the movie's greatest potential storylines.
reviews.author: Caitlin Chappell

reviews.text: At its best, Chazelle's film is a cinematic marvel, evidence enough that movies are magical, as it sweeps us into the beautiful, terrible world we recognise as Hollywood even now.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: Babylon is delightfully depraved with a completely committed cast chewing the silent era scenery.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle film’s direction is breathtaking and jaw-dropping...
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: "Babylon," therefore, represents an astonishing devolution of one of the industry’s heretofore most exciting, story-driven filmmakers.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: Babylon is cinematic vomit wrapped up in a pretty package. This movie stinks of being a phony, self-indulgent mess, but because of the pretty package, some people will insist that it's great.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: I encourage you to take the plunge.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: [A] lumpen, maudlin, misbegotten opus.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: An overwhelming, dazzling epic that sets fire to Hollywood while simultaneously celebrating all the joy it produces. Margot Robbie is a tornado of kinetic energy leveling everything in her path
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The core of Babylon’s central dilemma: It’s Singin’ in the Rain by way of Boogie Nights by way of Requiem for a Dream, a film that loves movies but hates what happens to the people who make them.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: “Babylon” is a deeply flawed movie, and its excesses often outshine its moments of stunning brilliance. There’s a masterpiece in here somewhere, if one can shovel through all the elephant dung.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Margot Robbie and Brad Pitt’s characters burn the candle at both ends in Damien Chazelle’s rollicking and ridiculous epic cautionary tale.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: Babylon is too high on its own supply, with Margot Robbie & Diego Calva carrying a film that’s overlong, overstuffed, and loses sight of its story.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: If Babylon is a failure, it’s a fabulous failure, and there are far too few of those today.
reviews.author: Rich Juzwiak

reviews.text: Shimmering, mournful, and riotous, Babylon is one of the year's best movies, thanks in part to a star-making performance by Diego Calva.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Just in time for the holidays! A relentless barrage of defecation, urination, regurgitation, ejaculation, fornication, asphyxiation, masturbation, exploitation, humiliation and overstimulation.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: La La Land on coke.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: Maybe how you feel about "Babylon" will depend on how steeped in irony your tears are when Nicole Kidman steps into frame under the AMC logo.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Babylon is not just another masterpiece from Chazelle, it is his magnum opus. It is a bold and risky move to challenge the identity of cinema through the form itself but the final result is undeniable.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: It’s a movie smitten with its own sense of grandeur and apparently pledged to the belief that the best way to depict unbridled decadence is to drown its audience in unbridled decadence.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: A three-hour movie that isn't boring for a second. Damien Chazelle elevates cinema by dragging it back to the gutter.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Like Kubrick, Damien Chazelle is working on 2 levels here. The party is real. But it is also an embodiment of the idea of how it feels to make a movie. The relentlessness. The hierarchies. The intense joy. The reality of what it takes to feed the machine.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: It's like Las Vegas in all its glamorous excess in a movie form. Boisterously and lavishly messy, ambitious, audacious... 'Babylon' is a shock and awe to the senses and outrageously engrossing.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle’s Babylon is a beautiful disaster of old school Hollywood proportions, but his fantasy commentary is woefully scattershot and the film a bloated mess.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Chazelle is so enamored with his simulacrum of this forgotten world that he loses sight of the people in it.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: The first 2 1/2 hours of Damien Chazelle's "Babylon" perfectly capture a singular vision of the silent film era that is rarely seen — irreverent, decadent, debauched. It's great filmmaking.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: Chazelle’s film operates in a single gear, stuffed with a lot of action but without much to say.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: Whatever emotions seeing a movie has ever made you feel, Chazelle finds a way to heighten the intensity. Another Oscar contender indeed with the way 'Babylon' speaks directly to a film lover's heart.
reviews.author: Catalina Combs

reviews.text: Chazelle’s latest film, Babylon, is the evil b-side to La La Land, where those sparkling dreams go to die. Los Angeles isn’t “la la land,” but a dark and dirty underbelly built on the backs of similar dreamers nearly 100 years prior.
reviews.author: Sophia Ciminello

reviews.text: Babylon is often pure mayhem, but it’s the beauty of life and film itself underneath that makes this one of the best movies about movies this year, and one of the best films of 2022.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: The unending madcap style lends to some hilarious moments, primarily when demonstrating the growing pains of advancing technology, but it’s only rarely amusing, made more discordant when the tone shifts all over the place.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: I have to give Chazelle credit because he goes for broke and shows little room for regret. Unfortunately, no matter how electric those first couple hours may prove, the third (yes, full third hour) can't help but drag.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle adds plenty of setpieces to Babylon like over-sweet chocolate chips, but the cake housing them is stale, underbaked and rotting.
reviews.author: Ankit Jhunjhunwala

reviews.text: A truly bizarre film that won’t be for everyone, but it will certainly leave a lasting impression on its viewers. It's a wild and crazy love letter to early Hollywood, and it isn't afraid to really push the envelope. The final scene is beautiful.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Many films have been made about the beginnings of the film industry, and the majority of them have been informative and entertaining, but Babylon is not one of them.
reviews.author: Kathia Woods

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle’s tribute to Old Hollywood is absolutely nuts in the best possibly way.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Babylon reviews itself when Jean Smart's character says, "it's a confluence of pure magic and bad taste."
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: A daring, formally audacious yet messy ode to cinema from one of the most enterprising filmmakers working today. Bravura and baffling in equal measure. Strap in.
reviews.author: Beth Webb

reviews.text: It begins to feel, as Babylon stretches out across three hours and eight minutes, that Chazelle has no clear idea where all of this is going.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Babylon is a ghastly, sticky, indulgent mess of a movie, slinging shock value in lieu of anything interesting to say.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Calva wears a poet’s heart on his sleeve, and beautifully so, while Robbie’s feral performance feels extracted from some higher plane of existence.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Even a full-blown fantasy needs its own eternal logic, a thing Babylon rarely gestures to or simply disregards completely.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Guaranteed to be a movie that will stay in your head, a swing-for-the-fences journey through an unimaginable rabbit hole of excess and jaw dropping behavior that stands alone in 2022 and more than earns its stripes.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: I can’t say I truly enjoyed watching “Babylon,” or that I’d ever want to see it again, but I definitely haven’t stopped thinking about it since screening it...
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: A combination of brightly lit bombast and casting-couch crud...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: The film’s propulsive energy is so authoritative that it occasionally threatens to nullify all other elements, but Robbie’s performance is equal to the task and bubbling with awards season kudos.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Chazelle swings for the fences, but Babylon feels like the worst kind of jazz: a loose freestyle comprised of beautiful moments punctuated by bum notes and off-key scatting.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: Burdened with the knowledge that this $80 million studio project could be the last of its kind, “Babylon” refracts Hollywood’s first major identity crisis through the prism of its latest one.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Babylon exposes it as the bittersweet lie it always was – showing an industry that’s corrupt... but also wily enough to disguise its own chew-’em-up-and-spit-’em-out business model as the very fairy tale that keeps the show on the road.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: The style might cause whiplash, but it’s worth it for the thrilling momentum Chazelle brings to his revisionist filmdom fantasia.
reviews.author: Neil Smith

reviews.text: It’s not the best movie you’ll see this year, but it’s the most movie by a long shot.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: It’s always a pleasure to be in the presence of such black-belt movie stars as Pitt and Robbie and there is something funny in Babylon’s wild, event-movie gigantism.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: No doubt plenty of cool kids will eagerly sign up to be pummeled by the film’s crazed excesses, though just as many will find it exhausting and sour. Even its technical virtuosity feels assaultive.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: The film is a down-in-the-muck advert for an ultimately dewy-eyed vision of the silver screen.
reviews.author: Keith Uhlich

reviews.text: Sometimes it’s dazzling, sometimes it’s derivative.Still, there are worse people to spend three hours with than Brad Pitt and Margot Robbie.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: “Babylon” is what movie love really looks like.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Even with a great turn from Brad Pitt, an impressive showing by newcomer Diego Calva and a bunch of entertaining cameos, the madcap comedy-drama can’t help but run out of creative crazy juice by the end as it unspools into cinematic sentimentality.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Babylon is a manic sprawl that only pretends to celebrate cinema. It’s really about prurience, dumb sensation, self-congratulation and willful ignorance of history.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: It just feels like Chazzelle is trying to do Baz Luhrmann — and, even more embarrassingly, he’s failing at it.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: The film makes bold swings that don’t always land, yet it’s not easily dismissable as a sensationalistic, ambitiously crammed, and wonderfully exhausting portrait of Hollywood.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Damien Chazelle's vibrant vision of 1920s Hollywood completely captures the cacophonous chaos of the era, while Margot Robbie turns in a towering powerhouse performance that may be her best yet, and in the dynamite and dashing Diego Calva, a star is born.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: A Raucous Ride Through Hollywood's Past.
reviews.author: Jeff Ewing

reviews.text: Deploying the "Whiplash" and "La La Land" filmmaker’s phenomenal creative passions, "Babylon" overflows from every cinematic orifice with bouncy music, flamboyant production value, and vivacious performances.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Babylon is a brash, bombastic, unwieldy comic opera conveyed with enough bad taste and directorial panache that it—refreshingly—registers as a refutation of the well-mannered prestige drama to which these kinds of nostalgic odes often conform.
reviews.author: Jordan Raup

reviews.text: Babylon is a daring Hollywood epic that utterly shocks the senses.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: That it’s crazily all-over-the-place and tonally scattershot is both a detriment and part of Babylon‘s charm
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Babylon is a cocaine-fueled journey that roars through the decadence and tomfoolery of the Golden Age. Rich with awe-inducing production design, costumes, score, and performances, the film is a glorious Hollywood epic set to rock cinema’s foundation.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Beautiful, troubled, and ephemeral, like a fever dream, but with enough reality to know the truth of the superficial nature of it's characters.
reviews.author: Bill Watters

reviews.text: A dazzling, dizzying cacophony of demented depravity. And yet the unrelenting, frenetic spectacle showcased through a Scorsese-inspired lens gives way to profundity, both sentimental and scorching.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: Babylon is an unwieldy yet wildly fun look at Hollywood's 1920's bacchanal days.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: A hyped-up cocaine conversation of a movie, throwing out lots of ideas and images and mammoth set pieces without ever amounting to anything.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: An exhilarating thrill to watch, though nobody should envy participating in what it depicts. The lifestyle is unsustainable, and even three hours of living it vicariously is exhausting, though rewarding, from the safety of the theater.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: The filmmaker throws everything he's got on the screen. Luckily, it all works. Bravo.
reviews.author: Alex Saveliev

reviews.text: It's truly exhausting and I hated watching it.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

synopsis: A tale of outsized ambition and outrageous excess, Babylon traces the rise and fall of multiple characters during an era of unbridled decadence and depravity in early Hollywood.
